title: Bonsai development: known issues and priorities
question: Which known issues are present in development?
answer: The tested development revision contains substantial access-control, data-preservation and core workflow problems. All known baseline issues are prioritized here, including those for which a separate local fix exists. The priority queue is assessed against unpatched development.
scope: Software behavior with synthetic records, generic account and persistence workflows, offline frozen parser fixtures, and read-only stored-result views. No fresh live analysis upload, analysis execution or curation write was performed for this report.
counting_rule: Distinct baseline issues and product-scope gaps are counted after the existing explicit alias merges. Local fix status is ignored. One local-only sidebar regression and one explained failed-QC case are excluded. Priorities are recommended release urgency, not observed clinical harm or a measure of product coverage.

priorities.P0: Resolve before ordinary-user access or restricted-data use. The record-privacy item is conditional on private records being a promised feature.
priorities.P1: Resolve before the affected workflow is released: unauthorized actions, lost or hidden information, incorrect selection, or a blocked normal workflow.
priorities.P2: Resolve in the next correction cycle, or defer with an explicit product decision and usable workaround.
priorities.P3: Presentation, accessibility or export-policy follow-up; raise priority if it is a release requirement.

first_actions: Review the ordinary/admin/uploader authorization matrix first, including both deletion routes and the ingestion boundary.
Settle the private-record contract before relying on its visibility marker. Private-group behavior is a separate boundary.
Prioritize group and metadata preservation, concurrent writes and stable comment identities before broad user testing.
Retest filtering, selected-only exports, saved-state feedback and all advertised result-reading paths on the eventual release build.

issues.title: Ordinary accounts can delete records
issues.observed: Both single and bulk API deletion use update permission, which ordinary accounts hold. The UI does not offer them deletion.
issues.why: Unauthorized destructive action crosses the documented role boundary.
issues.acceptance: Deny ordinary deletion before any service call; retain administrator deletion.

issues.title: The ingestion role boundary is inverted
issues.observed: The real baseline router admits user and rejects uploader in an isolated authorization test: observed statuses 201 and 401 respectively. The downstream service is a stub.
issues.why: A viewing role reaches the upload service while the intended automation role is blocked.
issues.acceptance: Require the intended write scope and verify the complete role matrix without executing ingestion.

issues.title: Private-record visibility is not enforced
issues.observed: An uninvited ordinary account can read an admin-owned private-marked record. The read function has no record-owner or visibility check.
issues.why: P0 if private records are promised; the source describes access fields as preparatory.
issues.acceptance: Agree the privacy contract, then enforce it across direct reads, lists and related routes, or disable the promise.

issues.title: Deleting a group removes unrelated memberships
issues.observed: Deleting one group removes a member's links to other groups. The record itself remains; membership aggregation returns edges outside the requested group.
issues.why: A routine organization action silently changes unrelated saved state.
issues.acceptance: Delete a populated group while retaining all records and every unrelated membership edge.

issues.title: Unchanged Apply removes undisplayed memberships
issues.observed: The selector displays common memberships, then treats them as each record's complete target set. Applying unchanged settings removes individual memberships.
issues.why: A no-change action causes persistent organization loss.
issues.acceptance: Apply the unchanged common selection and preserve every record's individual memberships.

issues.title: Concurrent metadata saves lose successful writes
issues.observed: Two isolated baseline appends both return success, but only one field remains. The read-modify-write operation replaces the complete metadata array.
issues.why: Reported success does not mean the user's data was retained.
issues.acceptance: Retain all independent concurrent fields; concurrent creation of one field must have one winner.

issues.title: Concurrent comments receive duplicate IDs
issues.observed: Five simultaneous baseline comments retain all five texts but receive one distinct ID. IDs are allocated from an unprotected prior snapshot.
issues.why: Later operations address comments by ID, so collisions make record management ambiguous.
issues.acceptance: Retain all texts with unique identifiers under forced simultaneous submissions.
sources: comment_id = max(c.id for c in comments)

issues.title: A stale editor overwrites an independent group edit
issues.observed: Saving a description in a stale second tab reverts the name saved in the first tab. Unchanged fields are resent in the full payload.
issues.why: Independent successful edits unexpectedly erase one another.
issues.acceptance: Save different fields from two tabs and retain both values.

issues.title: Appending valid metadata returns HTTP 500
issues.observed: Appending to a record with existing metadata mixes raw dictionaries and typed entries. Normal input fails instead of being appended.
issues.why: A core data-entry workflow is blocked for existing records.
issues.acceptance: Append valid fields while retaining originals; duplicate fields must get clear conflict feedback.

issues.title: Interleaved metadata categories hide fields
issues.observed: The view groups unsorted records by adjacent category, then overwrites a category when it appears again. Stored fields disappear from the rendered view.
issues.why: Users cannot reliably read all retained metadata.
issues.acceptance: Display every field when categories are interleaved in stored order.

issues.title: An accepted metadata table displays no contents
issues.observed: CSV-shaped metadata can be accepted and stored without conversion to the table read shape. The page then shows no columns or rows.
issues.why: Accepted input has no usable reading surface.
issues.acceptance: Show original headings and cells for both accepted CSV-shaped and stored-table representations.

issues.title: A normal empty CSV cell makes metadata unreadable
issues.observed: The baseline CSV reader retains a non-finite numeric value for an empty inventory cell. JSON serialization raises Out of range float values are not JSON compliant.
issues.why: Ordinary accepted data can break the record's reading route.
issues.acceptance: Accept missing cells and render the stored table without a serialization error.

issues.title: One confirmation saves, then reports a conflict
issues.observed: The original browser run saved a decision, returned HTTP 409 and displayed stale state. The baseline controller calls the creation service twice for one confirmation.
issues.why: Successful writes appear to fail, encouraging retries and obscuring saved state.
issues.acceptance: Call the service once and render refreshed saved state; verify with stubs before any separately scoped write test.

issues.title: Comment recovery duplicates a saved submission
issues.observed: A lost response can cause another append of the same comment. There is no request identity; an error before acceptance can also lose the draft.
issues.why: Retries can change persistent content while feedback remains uncertain.
issues.acceptance: A repeated identified request must store one comment; retain a draft after a known failed submission.

issues.title: Clearing selected-only rows leaves stale exports
issues.observed: After Select all, Show only selected and Deselect all, old rows remain visible. The later file check exported eight records with zero selected.
issues.why: The exported set can conflict with the user's visible selection intent.
issues.acceptance: At zero and nonzero selections, displayed rows and exported records must match the selected-only view.

issues.title: Select all adds an undefined extra target
issues.observed: A three-row table creates four local payload entries, including one without valid identifiers. The header checkbox is also handled as a row checkbox.
issues.why: Bulk actions receive an invalid extra target.
issues.acceptance: The header must select exactly the displayed valid row IDs, including after filtering; no write is needed for this check.

issues.title: The second numeric predicate overrides the first
issues.observed: Depth filtering replaces the prior frequency result instead of combining it. Three rows remain when the requested conjunction should return none.
issues.why: The table presents results outside the user's requested criteria.
issues.acceptance: Both predicates must intersect, including cases where either one fails.

issues.title: Hide dismissed crashes the detail page
issues.observed: The filter reads a legacy verified field before merging saved decisions. A record containing a rejected row returns HTTP 500.
issues.why: A normal saved-state filter makes the reading workflow unavailable.
issues.acceptance: Hide exactly the rejected rows using saved decision state, without changing stored decisions.

issues.title: Exact status filtering hides matching records
issues.observed: The status column is filterable but excluded from the search cache used by the advanced filter. A known matching row is omitted.
issues.why: The requested cohort can silently be incomplete.
issues.acceptance: Exact and combined status filters must return all expected records; clearing them must restore the full table.

issues.title: Membership preselection fails beyond 100 records
issues.observed: The UI sends one membership lookup for 125 selected records while the API permits at most 100 IDs. The common group is not preselected.
issues.why: Ordinary larger selections lose essential context before an edit.
issues.acceptance: Batch membership reads within the API limit and preselect the common group for all 125 records.

issues.title: A valid new account cannot be created
issues.observed: A normal unknown username produces the SDK's NotFoundError, while form validation catches the older HTTPError type. Creation returns HTTP 500.
issues.why: Administrator onboarding is blocked by the expected availability check.
issues.acceptance: Create and list one valid account; invalid fields must produce form feedback without a write.

issues.title: An existing account cannot be opened for editing
issues.observed: The edit form indexes a typed UserResponse as a dictionary. Opening an existing account returns HTTP 500.
issues.why: Normal account maintenance is unavailable.
issues.acceptance: Populate the form from the typed response and verify that an ordinary profile edit persists.

issues.title: Generic create/read routes disagree with the roles
issues.observed: The shared active-user dependency adds users:me to write-only uploader requests. The older list route requires write permission from ordinary readers.
issues.why: Supported automation and read workflows are blocked by unrelated scopes.
issues.acceptance: Allow generic uploader creation and ordinary list reads while preserving the intended denials.

issues.title: Old tabs retain the previous authenticated view
issues.observed: After logout or account switching, other tabs and browser history can retain the prior rendered page and access token. Independent profiles are a separate case.
issues.why: Shared-browser account changes leave stale authenticated state on screen.
issues.acceptance: Revalidate restored pages and coordinate account changes across tabs. Server-side token revocation is a separate contract.

issues.title: Basket names are interpreted as markup
issues.observed: A harmless b-tag record name becomes HTML in the basket. A missing optional assay also appears as the literal undefined label.
issues.why: Untrusted labels are not reliably presented as literal text. Script execution was not tested.
issues.acceptance: Render names literally and give a readable empty value for the optional assay.

issues.title: Private groups cannot be created with invitees
issues.observed: Creation accesses a nonexistent owner_id attribute. Group listing and direct lookup also apply a public-only visibility helper instead of honoring owner/invitee access.
issues.why: An advertised private-group workflow cannot be completed.
issues.acceptance: Owner and invitees must create, list and open the group; an uninvited account must be denied.

issues.title: A pending record cannot be opened
issues.observed: A valid record without a completed pipeline is accepted, but the summary assumes pipeline metadata exists and returns HTTP 500.
issues.why: A normal record lifecycle state has no usable page.
issues.acceptance: Empty and metadata-only records must open with clear pending feedback.

issues.title: Absent optional display metadata crashes a summary
issues.observed: The stored summary indexes optional resistance-level metadata that is absent in a valid stored decision. Rendering returns HTTP 500.
issues.why: Existing stored information cannot be read without changing the record.
issues.acceptance: Render the original summary and decisions when optional display fields are missing.

issues.title: Null stored results crash summary and detail pages
issues.observed: A valid null result is indexed as a dictionary in several reading helpers. Empty-result records cannot be opened reliably.
issues.why: A valid empty result becomes an application failure.
issues.acceptance: Keep stored null values and provide explicit availability feedback throughout both views.

issues.title: Unsupported stored data is presented as a negative
issues.observed: The detail route selects only TBProfiler results yet reports No predicted resistance determinants for a record with stored AMRFinder results.
issues.why: A missing reading surface is presented as absence of findings. Broader detail support also needs a scope decision.
issues.acceptance: Distinguish unavailable or unsupported results from a negative result; define supported detail types.

issues.title: Stored EMM results are omitted from the summary
issues.observed: The summary checks emmtype while current descriptors use emm. Stored results have no card, including explicit empty-result states.
issues.why: Supported parsed information never reaches its intended reading surface.
issues.acceptance: Display positive, empty and unavailable descriptors and preserve numeric zero values.

issues.title: Requested EMM table columns are silently absent
issues.observed: Two requested summary-column paths do not match the existing projection alias. Positive stored values are omitted even when those columns are requested.
issues.why: An explicitly requested table projection silently loses information.
issues.acceptance: Return the supplied type and cluster through both requested projection paths. Default layouts are a separate configuration choice.

issues.title: The extended summary lacks its record context
issues.observed: The imported card macro needs sample context when building a stored-row display link. Extended rendering returns HTTP 500 for the relevant record shape.
issues.why: The advertised extended view cannot be opened for valid stored content.
issues.acceptance: Open the display-only extended summary and retain its supplied rows and links without executing an analysis or viewer action.

issues.title: The configured EMM export fails
issues.observed: The formatter accesses the old descriptor field and old result-type name. Positive and empty EMM exports return HTTP 500 instead of a file.
issues.why: A configured release download path is blocked.
issues.acceptance: Produce CSV and TSV with correct record identity and supplied values, including defined empty results.

issues.title: A required companion file has no upload path
issues.observed: Frozen reports parse offline with their companion, but the original four API attempts returned HTTP 422. The upload route exposes no hAMRonization companion input.
issues.why: The supported Klebsiella paths have an incomplete ingestion contract.
issues.acceptance: Define and stub-test companion-file plumbing; verify ingestion separately before claiming the integration works.

issues.title: Selecting a single result type crashes Mykrobe parsing
issues.observed: Species-only and lineage-only requests raise UnboundLocalError although the full frozen report parses. Each branch needs its own result-type context.
issues.why: A supported parser request mode fails on valid input.
issues.acceptance: Selected values must match full-parse values while unrequested envelopes remain skipped.

issues.title: A header-only report has the wrong result shape
issues.observed: A valid empty table is marked parsed and returns a nested dictionary instead of the declared result list.
issues.why: Empty input violates the parser's output contract and can mislead downstream readers.
issues.acceptance: Return an empty envelope and empty list; retain numeric zero as a parsed value.

issues.title: A coverage stream silently loses rows
issues.observed: The baseline parser consumes its stream and reads it again. A two-row generic stream retains only the first row, while path input works.
issues.why: Accepted input is silently incomplete.
issues.acceptance: Read once and preserve both rows identically for path and stream input.

issues.title: Basket selections are shared across accounts
issues.observed: The next account inherits the prior basket, clearing it affects the first account, and another tab can retain stale contents.
issues.why: Selection intent is not isolated by account or synchronized reliably.
issues.acceptance: Keep independent account baskets, preserve same-account reloads and synchronize same-account tabs.

issues.title: A disabled session ends on a server-error page
issues.observed: The API denies the disabled account correctly, but frontend handling misses the current permission exception. Existing sessions return HTTP 500.
issues.why: Correct denial is obscured by broken session feedback; no successful bypass was observed.
issues.acceptance: End the inactive session clearly and show normal sign-in feedback.

issues.title: An unauthorized admin visit returns HTTP 500
issues.observed: The denial redirects to the nonexistent public.home endpoint. No administrative user data was displayed in the failed visit.
issues.why: An expected denial becomes a broken navigation/error page.
issues.acceptance: Return a usable denial or redirect with clear feedback.

issues.title: Ordinary users see a removal action that crashes
issues.observed: A regular account is offered Remove, but the API requires write permission and the frontend misses the SDK denial exception. The action returns HTTP 500.
issues.why: The available control disagrees with the role and produces misleading failure feedback.
issues.acceptance: Expose only permitted controls and handle a denied direct request without a server error.

issues.title: A populated editor says no records were added
issues.observed: The API has saved members, but the editor renders an empty samples list and displays No samples added yet.
issues.why: The edit screen contradicts the persisted membership.
issues.acceptance: Display the saved count or members and verify empty and populated states.

issues.title: Save and Reset remain active during a pending save
issues.observed: Repeated Save clicks produce overlapping writes. Reset and field changes remain possible during the two-stage operation.
issues.why: One user operation can launch competing updates and unclear feedback.
issues.acceptance: Guard repeated actions and use one captured payload until completion.

issues.title: Group failures hide partial or uncertain success
issues.observed: Core details can save while column settings fail. A lost success response gives the same generic Failed to save group message.
issues.why: The user cannot tell what persisted or what should be retried.
issues.acceptance: Report confirmed stages and uncertainty, preserve the draft and retry the same known group.

issues.title: A partial batch removal has no resumable intent
issues.observed: When one removal succeeds and another fails, refreshed common selection can become empty. Repeating Apply does not complete the original removal.
issues.why: The remaining membership needs individual review; unrelated-membership loss is a separate P1 issue.
issues.acceptance: Retain batch intent or expose per-record outcomes and a clear continuation path.

issues.title: Same-field edits silently use the last writer
issues.observed: Two editors can save different descriptions without a version precondition or conflict prompt. The later description replaces the earlier one.
issues.why: A concurrent overwrite is not distinguished from a normal successful edit.
issues.acceptance: Agree an edit-version/conflict contract and test stale updates.

issues.title: Session expiry discards an unsent comment draft
issues.observed: The form has no account-scoped draft recovery. The expiry observation was made on a layered candidate; the baseline likewise has no restoration path.
issues.why: Typed work can be lost during reauthentication. Exact baseline expiry feedback was not rerun.
issues.acceptance: Choose a draft-recovery policy and verify expiry, sign-in and account switching.

issues.title: Invalid metadata input returns a server failure
issues.observed: Empty batches and malformed CSV are not rejected cleanly before the write path. They return HTTP 500 rather than input feedback.
issues.why: Recoverable input mistakes look like application failures.
issues.acceptance: Reject invalid input with clear validation feedback and no record change.

issues.title: Missing-record links give broken or unrelated pages
issues.observed: Missing record, metadata, table and user-edit links can return HTTP 500, blank content or an unrelated redirect instead of a clear 404.
issues.why: Stale or incorrect links are difficult to diagnose and recover from.
issues.acceptance: Return a clear unavailable state without further dependent reads.

issues.title: SPA and SCCmec have no agreed summary surface
issues.observed: The fields are parsed and stored in the API but have no corresponding summary cards.
issues.why: A release-scope decision is missing. Raise to P1 if these reading surfaces are already promised.
issues.acceptance: Provide a supported reading surface or explicitly exclude the fields from the release claim.

issues.title: CSV protection misses formula-like sign prefixes
issues.observed: Harmless +1+1 and -1+1 names remain unprotected in CSV. Protection exists for other prefixes. Formula execution in a spreadsheet client was not tested.
issues.why: Export hardening is incomplete; raise to P1 for expected direct opening of untrusted CSV text.
issues.acceptance: Define and validate a spreadsheet-safe CSV contract for representative clients.

issues.title: The overview overflows phone-width screens
issues.observed: The original baseline page was 1488 CSS pixels wide at both 320 and 390 pixel viewports. The full page, rather than just the table, scrolls horizontally.
issues.why: Phone controls are awkward; raise priority if phone operation is required.
issues.acceptance: Contain horizontal scrolling inside the table and retain accessible page controls.

issues.title: A shortened version label has no full text label
issues.observed: The displayed database version is truncated. Its full value is present in the link URL but not in a title or accessible label.
issues.why: Reading the exact stored version requires inspecting or opening the link.
issues.acceptance: Expose the complete version as a readable title and accessible label.

issues.title: CSV export replaces name newlines with spaces
issues.observed: A quoted Unicode record name loses its embedded newline during export. Quoting, the accent and raw leading-zero identifiers are retained.
issues.why: Exact multiline fidelity is undefined; this is an export-contract decision.
issues.acceptance: Document the normalization or preserve multiline values consistently.

screenshots.title: A populated development group is presented as empty
screenshots.caption: Original baseline evidence for GROUP-EDITOR-EMPTY-COUNT. The finding records a 123-member group, but its edit screen says No samples added yet. The saved membership and its displayed empty state disagree.

screenshots.title: Combined numeric filters retain rows outside the requested conjunction
screenshots.caption: Original baseline evidence for VARIANT-FILTER-AND. The requested frequency/depth conjunction should exclude these rows. The second predicate overwrites the first predicate's result. Stored data was not altered by this filter check.

limits: This report is pinned to development 21eccf7 and the recorded SDK 5789a9c. No remote fetch or claim about later upstream changes is made.

The historical browser/API baseline, later layered observations and exact baseline source checks have different evidence strength. Each finding labels its basis; no fresh full development deployment was performed for this report.
The three SDK parser items apply to the recorded dependency revision. An installation using a different SDK revision must be checked separately.

Coverage includes 80 representative synthetic records across eight configured assay paths, including aliases, and table workflows up to 125 records. It is not exhaustive species or producer-version coverage.

The parser pass exercised 479 frozen reports and selected literal fields. Broader format/version combinations, real JASEN output, scientific correctness, LDAP/SSO, other browser engines and production-scale load remain untested.
Historical ingestion and curation-write failures are retained as evidence. No fresh live ingestion, curation write, sequencing workflow or clustering execution was performed for this report.

The local-only comment-sidebar context regression is excluded. The original failed-QC clustering case was explained and is also excluded. Existing reports and the running patched test instance are preserved.
